COMD 401.description: Public health issues related to speech, language, and hearing from local, national and global perspective in historical context. Special permission required by department.
COMD 401.subject: COMD
COMD 401.title: Public Health Perspective in Communication Sciences and Disorders

COMD 408.description: Directed readings and/or research in speech pathology.
COMD 408.subject: COMD
COMD 408.title: Directed Study in Speech and Language Pathology

COMD 500.description: Human communication disorders with an overview of prevention and treatment programs.
COMD 500.subject: COMD
COMD 500.title: Introduction to Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology

COMD 501.description: An intensive study of the anatomy and physiology of the speech and hearing mechanisms.
COMD 501.subject: COMD
COMD 501.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Hearing Mechanisms

COMD 503.description: Detailed examination of the anatomy and physiology of the auditory and vestibular system.
COMD 503.subject: COMD
COMD 503.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Auditory and Vestibular System

COMD 507.description: Study of language theory and international phonetics alphabet transcription.
COMD 507.subject: COMD
COMD 507.title: Language Theory and Phonetics

COMD 521.description: Diagnostic and therapeutic programs for the communicatively handicapped will be observed in the public school and various rehabilitative settings. Discussion and study of basic therapeutic theories and procedures utilized in speech therapy. Introduction to phonetics or equivalent or permission of instructor.
COMD 521.subject: COMD
COMD 521.title: Introduction to Clinical Procedures in Speech Pathology

COMD 525.description: Presentation of current experimental or innovative programs in diagnosis and treatment of the communicatively impaired. Course is designed to update the practicing clinician in specific areas of expertise. May be repeated for credit. Individual topics to be announced by title. Permission of instructor.
COMD 525.subject: COMD
COMD 525.title: Selected Topics

COMD 526.description: The diagnosis and treatment of articulation problems in children and adults, including analysis of current research in testing and therapy for articulation disorders.
COMD 526.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in COMD 501 and C or better in COMD 507 or equivalents.
COMD 526.subject: COMD
COMD 526.title: Disorders of Articulation: Evaluation and Therapy

COMD 540.description: Basic anatomy and psycho-physics of hearing, the pathologies of hearing loss, introduction to identification procedures including organization of hearing conservation programs and practice in pure-tone audiometry, and impact of hearing loss on preschool and school-age children and educational, psychological, and medical aspects of habilitation.
COMD 540.subject: COMD
COMD 540.title: Principles of Audiology

COMD 560.description: Introduction to the clinical process through observation of various diagnostic reports and intervention programs included.
COMD 560.subject: COMD
COMD 560.title: Observation of Speech Language Pathology

COMD 570.description: The language acquisition process in normal children, including the development of semantics, morphology, syntax, phonology, and pragmatics; American dialects and bilingualism.
COMD 570.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in COMD 501 and C or better in COMD 507.
COMD 570.subject: COMD
COMD 570.title: Introduction to Language Development

COMD 700.description: Study of advanced alternative procedures for the evaluation and management of individuals with significant phonological disturbances.
COMD 700.subject: COMD
COMD 700.title: Advanced Seminars in Speech Sound Disorders

COMD 701.description: An introduction to the problem of stuttering; its possible causes; the management and training of clients.
COMD 701.subject: COMD
COMD 701.title: Stuttering: Evaluation and Therapy

COMD 702.description: Nature, diagnosis and treatment of cleft palate and craniofacial anomalies.
COMD 702.subject: COMD
COMD 702.title: Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Disorders: Evaluation and Management

COMD 703.description: Genetic factors that contribute to disorders of speech, language, and hearing.
COMD 703.subject: COMD
COMD 703.title: Genetics of Communication Disorders

COMD 704.description: The diagnosis and treatment of voice disorders in children and adults. The neurological, physiological, and psychological bases of voice disorders will be considered.
COMD 704.subject: COMD
COMD 704.title: Disorders of Voice: Evaluation and Therapy

COMD 705.description: The course is designed to introduce students to the neuropathological bases for acquired communicative, language and motor speech disorders in adults. The course includes information about the differential diagnosis of adult language and cognitive disorders as well as clinical intervention techniques.
COMD 705.subject: COMD
COMD 705.title: Adult Speech and Language Disorders

COMD 706.description: Components of communication, oral language, and speech in preschool children with diverse problems across all aspects of language learning, including factors that serve as precursors to literacy skills as well as evidence-based approaches to language assessment and intervention.
COMD 706.subject: COMD
COMD 706.title: Preschool Language Development and Disorders

COMD 707.description: Assigned readings and reports combined with clinical practice in the evaluation of cases in areas such as aphasia, cerebral palsy, voice disorders, articulation problems, stuttering, or cleft palate.
COMD 707.subject: COMD
COMD 707.title: Clinical Evaluation in Communicative Disorders

COMD 708.description: Directed readings and/or research in speech pathology. May be repeated for credit.
COMD 708.subject: COMD
COMD 708.title: Directed Study in Speech Pathology

COMD 709.description: Pre- and postoperative clinical management of the laryngeal patient with emphasis on communication and related problems.
COMD 709.subject: COMD
COMD 709.title: Laryngectomy Clinical Management

COMD 710.description: Individually assigned directed readings in speech pathology. May be repeated for credit when the topics covered or subject matter is different.
COMD 710.subject: COMD
COMD 710.title: Selected Topics in Speech Pathology

COMD 711.description: An in-depth study of selected issues. May be repeated for credit when the topics covered or subject matter is different.
COMD 711.subject: COMD
COMD 711.title: Seminar in Speech Pathology

COMD 712.description: A study of management systems in funding, scheduling, and case load.
COMD 712.subject: COMD
COMD 712.title: Management and Coordination of Programs in Speech Pathology and Audiology

COMD 713.description: Neurocognitive bases for speech and language in the central nervous system, includ-ing anatomy and physiology and clinical management of the neurogenic speech dis-orders. Major emphasis on neuroanatomy and neurophysiology, signs and symptoms, etiology, and the diagnosis and treatment of motor speech disorders.
COMD 713.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in COMD 501.
COMD 713.subject: COMD
COMD 713.title: Neurophysiology and Motor Speech Disorders

COMD 714.description: Aging, communicative processes and problems associated with aging, and specific communicative disorders associated with aging. Methods of assessment and rehabilitation will be considered.
COMD 714.subject: COMD
COMD 714.title: Gerontology and Communicative Disorders

COMD 715.description: A study of historical perspectives, current issues, assessment, intervention techniques, and training strategies in augmentative communication.
COMD 715.subject: COMD
COMD 715.title: Augmentative Communication: Assessment and Intervention

COMD 716.description: Public health issues and historical context related to speech, language, and hearing from local, national and global perspectives.
COMD 716.subject: COMD
COMD 716.title: Public Health Perspectives in Communication Sciences and Disorders

COMD 717.description: Issues affecting speech-language pathologists including professional education, certification, licensure, legislation, standards, and ethics.
COMD 717.subject: COMD
COMD 717.title: Professional Issues in Speech-Language Pathology

COMD 720.description: The relationship between oral and written language and factors that impact reading and writing (phonological awareness, phonics, vocabulary). Reading (word-level, comprehension, fluency) and writing (composition, spelling) development, assessment, intervention and issues related to delivery of literacy services in the schools.
COMD 720.subject: COMD
COMD 720.title: School-Age Language Literacy Development and Disorders

COMD 721.description: This course is an introduction to the area of cognitive reorganization after traumatic brain injury as well as in dementia. Assessment of cognitive functioning as well as cognitive reorganization techniques and their applications will be described.
COMD 721.subject: COMD
COMD 721.title: Cognitive Disorders and Reorganization

COMD 722.description: Anatomical and physiological orientation to typical and disordered feeding and swallowing across the lifespan, including interprofessional education for roles and responsibilities of allied and medical health partners involved in patient care.
COMD 722.subject: COMD
COMD 722.title: Feeding and Swallowing Disorders: Evaluation and Therapy

COMD 723.description: Diagnosis and treatment of communication problems in adolescent children, including educational psychosocial sequelae.
COMD 723.subject: COMD
COMD 723.title: Language Disorders in Adolescents

COMD 724.description: Practical application skills for speech-language pathology in the medical setting.
COMD 724.subject: COMD
COMD 724.title: Introduction to Medical Speech-Language Pathology

COMD 725.description: Anatomical and physiological orientation to typical and disordered pediatric feeding and swallowing from birth to 18 years of age, including interprofessional education for roles and responsibilities of allied and medical health partners involved in patient care.
COMD 725.subject: COMD
COMD 725.title: Pediatric Feeding and Swallowing Disorders: Evaluation and Therapy

COMD 726.description: Issues in traumatic brain injury and implications for speech and language function.
COMD 726.subject: COMD
COMD 726.title: Advanced Cognitive Retraining

COMD 727.description: Theories of reading development with regard to their implications for assessment and intervention. Connections between oral and written language skills, including vocabulary as a link between word level and text-level skills. Overall framework for thinking about literacy as a multi-component language skill.
COMD 727.subject: COMD
COMD 727.title: Advanced Study of Literacy for Speech-Language Pathologists

COMD 728.description: Foundations in culturally responsive clinical practice, including frameworks for cross-cultural engagement, evidence-based practice in multilingualism and dialectal variation, neurodiversity, power dynamics and marginalization, and related topics. Content is relevant to assessment and intervention in clinical practice.
COMD 728.subject: COMD
COMD 728.title: Cultural Responsiveness in Clinical Practice

COMD 735.description: The use of counseling skills by speech-language pathologists regarding the impact of communication disorders on the family system, the importance of interpersonal communication in counseling, and the principles and processes of counseling in facilitating behavior change.
COMD 735.subject: COMD
COMD 735.title: Counseling in Speech-Language Pathology

COMD 738.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition that affects 1 in 44 children in the United States. Speech-language pathologists are key team members in the assessment and treatment of individuals with ASD. This graduate level elective course is an introduction to ASD for the speech-language-pathologist, and is intended to prepare speech-language pathologists to understand and serve this unique population. Content areas will include: diagnostic criteria and assessment, etiology, language and communication strengths and weaknesses, speech and language assessment for the individual with ASD, and ASD interventions targeting language and communication.
COMD 738.subject: COMD
COMD 738.title: Introduction to Autism for the Speech-Language Pathologist

COMD 744.description: Neurocognitive bases for speech and language in the central nervous system including anatomy and physiology and theoretical constructs of language.
COMD 744.subject: COMD
COMD 744.title: Neurocognitive Bases of Language Behavior

COMD 745.description: The physical and related psychological attributes of speech. Use of electronic instruments and laboratory practices in measurement of acoustic variables. Introduction to information theory.
COMD 745.subject: COMD
COMD 745.title: Introduction to Speech Science and Acoustic Measurement

COMD 748.description: Communication options and dysphagia management for speech-language pathologists working with tracheostomized patients.
COMD 748.subject: COMD
COMD 748.title: Speech Pathology Management of Patients with Tracheostomy Ventilator Dependency

COMD 750.description: Basic anatomy and psycho-physics of hearing, pathologies of hearing loss, introduction to identification procedures including hearing screening and pure-tone audiometry, impact of hearing loss on preschool and school-aged children, and educational, psychological, and medical aspects of auditory habilitation.
COMD 750.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in COMD 507.
COMD 750.subject: COMD
COMD 750.title: Introduction to Audiology and Aural Habilitation

COMD 754.description: Effects of hearing loss on a child's development and also on adult function and quality of life (linguistic, intellectual, social, and educational). Communication assessment and case management, including parent and patient training, education, and counseling.
COMD 754.subject: COMD
COMD 754.title: Aural (Re)Habilitation of Children and Adults

COMD 755.description: Comprehensive rehabilitation of hearing-impaired adults with emphasis upon amplification, auditory training, and speech reading in developing communication skills.
COMD 755.subject: COMD
COMD 755.title: Aural Rehabilitation of Adults

COMD 760.description: Anatomy and physiology of the normal cochlea and the eighth cranial nerve. Evoked otoacoustic emissions as a diagnostic medium. Cochlear pathology with emphasis on candidacy for cochlear implantation.
COMD 760.subject: COMD
COMD 760.title: Cochlear Implants

COMD 761.description: Clinical techniques for the communication assessment and habilitation of the child post cochlear implantation.
COMD 761.subject: COMD
COMD 761.title: Habilitation of Individuals with Cochlear Implants

COMD 762.description: Basic sign vocabulary for speech-language pathologists’ professional use with hearing-impaired clients. Focus on the nature and components of manual language systems.
COMD 762.subject: COMD
COMD 762.title: Aural Habilitation: Manual Communication

COMD 772.description: Supervised clinical practice in screening, diagnosis, and therapy.
COMD 772.subject: COMD
COMD 772.title: Practicum in Speech Language Pathology and Audiology

COMD 774.description: Supervised internship in diagnosis and treatment of children and adults with communicative disorders in clinical and public school settings in field situations.
COMD 774.subject: COMD
COMD 774.title: Internship in Speech Pathology

COMD 790.description: An introduction to research methods applicable to and utilized in speech pathology and audiology. An analysis of basic and applied research.
COMD 790.subject: COMD
COMD 790.title: Research and Evidence Based Practice in Communication Sciences and Disorders

COMD 791.description: Preparation of research designs, procedures of sampling and use of statistical measures.
COMD 791.subject: COMD
COMD 791.title: Research Methodology

COMD 800.description: An in depth exploration of problems, theories, and research in a specific area of speech pathology. May be repeated for credit when the topic(s) covered is different. Individual topics to be announced with title.
COMD 800.subject: COMD
COMD 800.title: Seminar in Speech Pathology

COMD 801.description: A series of lectures, presentations, and discussion sessions in a selected area of speech pathology. May be repeated for credit when the topic(s) covered is different. Individual topics to be announced with title.
COMD 801.subject: COMD
COMD 801.title: Advanced Topics in Speech Pathology

COMD 802.description: Issues of local, state, and national import related to the prevention or solution of problems in speech pathology.
COMD 802.subject: COMD
COMD 802.title: Contemporary Issues In Speech Pathology

COMD 803.description: Introduction to nonlinear phonological theory (e.g., autosegmental, metrical) and its application for assessment and intervention of children with phonological disorders.
COMD 803.subject: COMD
COMD 803.title: Advanced Study of Clinical Phonology

COMD 805.description: Theories of language processing, language development, and the effects of neural pathology on the normal language process.
COMD 805.subject: COMD
COMD 805.title: Advanced Study of Language Disorders in Adults

COMD 810.description: Seminar-format orientation to key issues related to preparing for academic career including the responsible conduct of research, career development, and skills required for success in academia. Content varies; topics announced in advance. Required to be repeated for 4 hours of credit to fulfill COMD Doctoral Program Curriculum requirements.
COMD 810.subject: COMD
COMD 810.title: Professional Seminar in Communication Sciences and Disorders

COMD 811.description: Seminar-format orientation to the breadth of research in COMD. This seminar will introduce students to a variety of lines of research, populations, research designs, methods, and models. Content varies; topics announced in advance. Required to be repeated for 2 hours of credit to fulfill COMD Doctoral Program Curriculum requirements.
COMD 811.subject: COMD
COMD 811.title: Survey of Research in COMD

COMD 812.description: This course provides structured training in scientific writing, with emphasis on manuscripts, grant proposals, and article critiques.
COMD 812.subject: COMD
COMD 812.title: Scientific Writing in COMD: Papers Grants

COMD 815.description: Mentored teaching experience emphasizing course design and preparation, student engagement, classroom management, use of learning management systems, and assessment.
COMD 815.subject: COMD
COMD 815.title: Mentored Teaching in COMD

COMD 820.description: Advanced study of the physical and related psychological attributes of sound and measurement of acoustic variables of sound and speech. Review of current research in speech science.
COMD 820.subject: COMD
COMD 820.title: Advanced Speech Science

COMD 821.description: The normal auditory system; middle ear and cochlear physiology as determiners of auditory psychophysics.
COMD 821.subject: COMD
COMD 821.title: Advanced Hearing Science

COMD 822.description: Processes underlying speech production, including neural control, respiration, phonation, and articulation; theories explaining the processes; measurements of physical properties of speech.
COMD 822.subject: COMD
COMD 822.title: Normal Bases of Speech Production

COMD 823.description: Advanced study of the effects of pathology on the normal language processes. Theories of language processing and development over the life span. Effects of focal and diffuse neutral pathologies on language processes.
COMD 823.subject: COMD
COMD 823.title: Normal Bases of Language

COMD 827.description: The course focuses on prominent theories and contemporary research on the relation between oral and written language processing in skilled adults, the development of oral and written language abilities in children, and developmental and acquired disorders of language and reading.
COMD 827.subject: COMD
COMD 827.title: Connections between Oral and Language Literacy

COMD 890.description: Seminar-format orientation to key issues related to teaching for doctoral students preparing for an academic career. Topics covered will span from theories and principles of adult learning through the major aspects of course development and teaching.
COMD 890.subject: COMD
COMD 890.title: Teaching Fundamentals in Communication Sciences and Disorders
